_meta.what: Nine 3-D meshes generated from user-supplied photographs by tencent/Hunyuan3D-2 (/shape_generation), for testing a mesh -> metric-tree extraction pipeline.
_meta.why_these: They are GENERATED meshes at 175k-599k faces, not hand-modelled low-poly assets. Extraction code is commonly calibrated on the latter and only ever fed the former; this set is the former.

generator.note: seed pinned and randomize_seed disabled, so these meshes are reproducible from the same photos

_meta.how_to_score: Score leaf counts against anatomy_ground_truth.expected_feature_count. Do NOT score against any reference count your own pipeline derives from its own skeleton -- that closes a loop in which discarding half the animal RAISES the score.
_meta.convention: One Metric Tree leaf per distinct TERMINAL APPENDAGE: each arm, leg, wing, tentacle or ray counts one; the head counts one; the tail counts one when the animal has an external tail. Sub-flap detail (digits, antennae, ears, eyes, fins that are not skeletal limbs) is NOT counted -- it is not a uniaxial-base flap at this scale. This is the convention the five committed subjects already follow (humanoid: 2 arms + 2 legs + head = 5; quadruped: 4 legs + head + tail = 6), restated here from anatomy rather than inherited from an extraction run.
_meta.ground_truth_source: fixtures/anatomy_expectation.json from AI-Driven-Origami-IDE; human-authored from published anatomy, each row carrying its own derivation and citation. Nothing in it is computed from any extraction.

anatomy_ground_truth.derivation: 6 legs + head + gaster = 8. Applies the SPIDER PRECEDENT: the mass the legs attach to is the hub (there, the cephalothorax; here, the mesosoma) and the free axial mass is a flap (there, the opisthosoma; here, the gaster, joined by a narrow petiole and unambiguously free). That reasoning is topological, not taxonomic, so it carries from arachnid to insect. Antennae excluded. Ruled by the repository owner 2026-09-08; proposal and the alternatives considered: docs/superpowers/decisions/2026-09-08-s8-corpus-proposal.md.
anatomy_ground_truth.citation: Wikipedia, 'Ant': family Formicidae, six legs; the gaster is connected to the mesosoma by a narrow petiole.

anatomy_ground_truth.derivation: 8 legs + metasoma (tail) = 9. The prosoma is the hub, exactly as the spider's cephalothorax, and scorpions have no head distinct from it. THE PINCERS ARE PEDIPALPS AND ARE EXCLUDED -- the spider row already rules pedipalps sub-flap detail, and consistency outranks how visually dominant they are. A reader who counts them reaches 11.
anatomy_ground_truth.citation: Wikipedia, 'Scorpion': order Scorpiones, eight legs, a pair of grasping pedipalps bearing chelae, and a narrow segmented metasoma ending in a telson.

anatomy_ground_truth.derivation: 10 legs = 10. Decapods bear five pairs of pereiopods and THE CHELAE ARE THE FIRST PAIR -- modified walking legs, a different appendage from the pedipalps the spider row excludes. The cephalothorax is the hub and the abdomen is reduced and folded beneath it, so it is not a free axial flap; there is no distinct head and no external tail. Ruled by the repository owner 2026-09-08; proposal and the alternatives considered: docs/superpowers/decisions/2026-09-08-s8-corpus-proposal.md.
anatomy_ground_truth.citation: Wikipedia, 'Crab' and 'Decapoda': ten pereiopods, the first pair bearing chelae; in Brachyura the abdomen is reduced and folded under the cephalothorax.
